# Inventory Visibility Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Inventory Visibility Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 6 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm licensing for your tenant and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness. Building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved inventory environment, publisher prefix and maker access. Confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available; keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded inventory files, the proposed inventory feed, reference data, Microsoft Teams and the intended channel. Document blocked paths; do not bypass them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always authentication trigger. Record who may build, test and later use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for the read-only ERP or commerce inventory feed and the warehouse and store reference data. No customer connection is needed for the synthetic workshop. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare planner, store-manager, category-manager and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment. Makers use Draft Preview; do not publish to enable sharing. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: the Copilot Studio browser and reviewed files, with no PAC CLI or YAML import. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Planning-rule ownership | Have the inventory owner approve real targets, safety stock, lead times and costs before replacing the fixed synthetic planning inputs. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Inventory business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Availability reconciliation and exception review work by location and SKU. Agree where planners lose time reconciling availability before judging stockout, overstock, lead-time and channel reviews.

Fill your baseline record:

| Location | SKU or category | Measurement period | Availability checks | Stockout or overstock events | Verification source | Review owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree inventory replacement connections, governance, support, telemetry and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Inventory business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Inventory business owner | Approve inventory sources, planning scope and the review workflow; agree production success measures without treating synthetic quantities as results. |
| Authorized inventory approvers | Verify quantities in the system of record and decide any transfer, replenishment or allocation outside the agent. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the owned agent in Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm tenant licensing and capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any inventory connection is approved. |
| Inventory data connection owners | Approve the read-only inventory feed and warehouse and store reference data; record connection identities and least-privilege references. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check IV-01 through IV-04 and the boundary tests on the current Draft; fail cases with absent identifiers and stop comparisons without Easy/Manual parity. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route inventory decisions to authorized approvers. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Inventory replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures have named agreement.
- [ ] The inventory owner records current availability reconciliation and exception review work before choosing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/inventory-visibility/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and publisher prefix are approved before any build lane starts.
- [ ] The customer confirms authenticated audience and least-privilege access for inventory, cost and price information.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/inventory-visibility/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/inventory-visibility/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/inventory-visibility/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/inventory-visibility/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Inventory Visibility Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_inventory-visibility-rules-and-safety.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_inventory-visibility-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: channel-allocation
9. Add skill: inventory-dashboard
10. Add skill: replenishment-plan
11. Add skill: stock-alerts
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass IV-01: Inventory Planner
15. Pass IV-02: Store Manager
16. Pass IV-03: Inventory Planner
17. Pass IV-04: Category Manager
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: IV-01, IV-02, IV-03, IV-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If this lane is chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `InventoryVisibilityAgent` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] The optional Brainstem lane is recorded as used or skipped; no workshop step depends on it.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Each unchanged inventory prompt passes once in a separate fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] The deterministic validator judges each full response; annotated screenshots do not replace the machine gate.
- [ ] Any Easy/Manual comparison uses identical instructions, knowledge, skills, model and case identifiers.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before showing inventory, cost or price information. Request only the read scopes needed for approved inventory and reference data. Restrict the audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Approved read-only ERP or commerce inventory feed

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Inventory data connection owners

1. **Bind Approved read-only ERP or commerce inventory feed — read:** Bind scoped read-only connector or API actions.

2. **Identity for Approved read-only ERP or commerce inventory feed:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved read-only ERP or commerce inventory feed:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved read-only ERP or commerce inventory feed:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 4](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Make no inventory promise; the quantity is synthetic and needs system-of-record verification. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return a scenario or review candidate; any write needs authenticated tools, authorization, audit and explicit approval.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Approved warehouse and store reference data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Inventory data connection owners

1. **Bind Approved warehouse and store reference data — read:** Add governed reference data as approved knowledge or read-only actions.

2. **Identity for Approved warehouse and store reference data:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved warehouse and store reference data:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved warehouse and store reference data:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 7](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Send no message; return the review candidates only, because the package has no Teams action. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return a scenario or review candidate; any write needs authenticated tools, authorization, audit and explicit approval.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Microsoft Teams

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Inventory data connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams — write:** Keep outputs unsent; gate any posting or review workflow behind approval (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 7](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Send no message; return the review candidates only, because the package has no Teams action. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return a scenario or review candidate; any write needs authenticated tools, authorization, audit and explicit approval.

### Step 3-4. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Inventory data connection owners

Create dedicated read-only references for the approved inventory feed and reference data; verify least-privilege access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Approved connections preserve the reviewed input and output contract; no live lookup or update is claimed without tool evidence.
- [ ] Authenticated tools, authorization checks, audit logging and explicit human approval are in place before any inventory write.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Before rollout, test an approved test deployment as planners, store and category managers and an unshared identity; maker access does not prove user access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data measures; fixed synthetic targets, safety stock, lead times and costs are not production thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked inventory corpus | All four cases, IV-01 through IV-04, include every required marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; no tools or web search. |
| Read-only inventory boundary | Any reservation, transfer, replenishment, allocation, promise, sale or purchase is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Require a positive target-state anchor without a blocker or refusal; withhold reshoot-required images. |
| Release state | The owned workshop agent is Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Inventory business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Inventory business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved inventory audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review failed inventory sessions, their transcripts, tool connection and authentication errors, and credit use in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.
